title: Germany Building Fire : Three Indian students from Keralam killed

Indian students from Keralam killed in Germany building fire
BERLIN: Three Indian students from Keralam were killed and five other people injured after a fire broke out at a residential building in Bochum, Germany, early on October 13, Tuesday. German authorities have provisionally arrested a 41-year-old Romanian national who lived in the same building on suspicion of murder, as investigators probe whether the blaze was deliberately set. The Indian Embassy in Berlin has confirmed the deaths and said that it is coordinating with local authorities to assist the affected families.
Three Indian nationals (two women and one man) have tragically lost their lives in a fire incident in Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. All 3 were studying in Germany.

The victims were identified as Anjali Sheela Joy from Kollam district, Sivin Johny from Ernakulam district and Nova Sabu from Idukki district. The three, comprising two women aged 25 and 27 and a 26-year-old man, were studying in Germany, according to the Indian Embassy in Berlin.
In a post on X on October 13, Wednesday, the embassy expressed its condolences to the families and confirmed that the incident was under investigation by German authorities. “Three Indian nationals (two women and one man) have tragically lost their lives in a fire incident in Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. All 3 were studying in Germany”, the embassy said.
It added that the Embassy of India in Berlin and the Consulate General of India in Frankfurt were in contact with local authorities and the bereaved families, extending all necessary assistance. “We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families in this hour of grief”, the embassy said.
Three young Indian students have lost their lives in a horrific fire at a residential building in Bochum, Germany.
